reason: The hypothesis relies on the premise that carbon doping forms Cr/V-sequestering carbides, but the cited evidence (E1, E2) does not demonstrate this in the WTaCrV system. E1 only notes general carbide growth at defects, and E2 confirms Cr/V precipitation in the unmodified alloy but provides no data on carbon effects. The key mechanistic premises are thus unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Carbon doping will form carbides that sequester Cr and V.
Carbide sequestration reduces thermodynamic driving force for radiation-induced Cr/V precipitation.
Carbides act as defect sinks, maintaining low irradiation hardening.
Unmodified alloy forms 3-5 nm Cr/V-rich precipitates at ~8 dpa, 1050 K.
